_source: groundSpring Exp 015: Sensor noise propagation through Anderson localization to QS regime prediction
_references: Dong et al. (2020) 'Calibration and validation of soil moisture sensors' Agriculture 10:598
Bourgain & Kachkovskiy (2018) 'Anderson localization for two interacting quasiperiodic particles' GAFA 29:3-43
Allen et al. (1998) FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56

_provenance.notes: Propagates Exp 001 sensor noise through Anderson localization (Exp 008) to predict QS regime confidence intervals. Combines three validated modules: decompose, anderson, rarefaction.
_provenance.data_origin: Derived from Dong et al. 2020 sensor calibration + Anderson analytical model
_provenance.real_data_accession: Dong et al. 2020 (10.3390/agriculture10120598) Table 3 sensor calibration

sensor_noise.description: Soil moisture sensor noise from Exp 001 (Dong et al. 2020)

anderson_model.description: 1D Anderson localization model for QS signal propagation

propagation.description: Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation: sensor noise → θ → W_eff → γ → ξ

localization_length_cv_cs616.description: CV of localization length due to CS616 noise (lower noise → lower CV)

localization_length_cv_ec5.description: CV of localization length due to EC5 noise (higher noise → higher CV)

bias_corrected_improvement.description: Bias correction reduces uncertainty when operating in the non-saturated disorder regime. At high W (saturated γ), improvement is minimal — the physics dominates sensor quality. Tolerance of -0.15 accounts for Monte Carlo variance at n_mc=200: bias removal can increase CV when the bias contribution to total error is small relative to MC sampling noise (σ_improvement ≈ 0.08 at n=200).
